questions.questionText: Your team needs to visualize the historical CPU and memory utilization of several Compute Engine virtual machines to determine if they need to be resized. Which Google Cloud service provides the built-in dashboards and metric storage for this requirement?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Monitoring is the core observability service used to collect, store, and visualize performance metrics (like CPU, memory, and disk usage) for Google Cloud resources via dashboards.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Logging: Cloud Logging is used for storing and analyzing event logs and text records, not for natively graphing continuous performance metrics.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace provides distributed tracing to analyze latency across microservices, not general infrastructure hardware metrics.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler analyzes CPU and memory usage at the code/function level inside an application, not general VM infrastructure utilization.

questions.questionText: Your company’s security team requires that all application logs be retained for three years and be available for complex SQL-based auditing and analysis. What is the most appropriate log routing destination?
options: Route logs to a Cloud Storage bucket using Archive storage class
Keep the logs in the _Default log bucket

explanation.general explanation: Routing logs to BigQuery is the ideal pattern when you need to perform complex, structured SQL queries on log data for auditing and analytics over a long retention period.

why other options are wrong.Route logs to a Cloud Storage bucket usi: While Cloud Storage is great for cheap long-term retention, it does not natively support complex SQL-based analysis without loading the data elsewhere or using external engines.
why other options are wrong.Route logs to Cloud Pub/Sub: Pub/Sub is used for real-time streaming of logs to third-party tools (like Splunk); it is not a long-term storage or querying database.
why other options are wrong.Keep the logs in the _Default log bucket: The _Default log bucket retains logs for 30 days by default (though it can be customized), but it does not provide the advanced analytical SQL capabilities of BigQuery.

questions.questionText: You are running a complex microservices architecture on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Users are reporting that requests are occasionally taking over 5 seconds to complete. You need to visualize the exact path of a request and see which specific microservice is causing the delay. Which tool should you use?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Trace is a distributed tracing system that collects latency data from your applications and displays it in near real-time. It allows you to track a single request as it propagates through various microservices to identify latency bottlenecks.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler is used to identify functions in your code that consume high CPU or RAM continuously. It does not track the lifecycle or latency of an individual HTTP request across services.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Monitoring: Cloud Monitoring shows aggregate metrics, not the step-by-step latency breakdown of an individual distributed user request.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Logging: While logs might contain timestamps, piecing them together manually to find latency across microservices is extremely difficult compared to the visual waterfall provided by Cloud Trace.

questions.questionText: A Java application running on Compute Engine frequently crashes due to OutOfMemory (OOM) errors in production. You need to identify exactly which functions or methods in your code are consuming the most RAM. Which Google Cloud service provides this continuous analysis with minimal overhead?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Profiler continuously gathers CPU and memory usage data from your production applications. It provides a visual flame graph that points directly to the specific methods and functions in your code that are consuming the most resources.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace analyzes the latency of requests across services, not the internal RAM consumption of specific code functions.
why other options are wrong.Error Reporting: Error Reporting groups and alerts on crashes and exceptions, but it does not continuously profile memory allocation leading up to an OOM crash.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Monitoring: Cloud Monitoring will show that the VM's memory is high, but it cannot peer inside the Java Virtual Machine to tell you which specific code function is allocating the memory.

questions.questionText: To meet strict regulatory compliance, your financial institution must retain all Admin Activity audit logs for 7 years. These logs will rarely be accessed, but must be preserved at the lowest possible cost. Which observability integration pattern should you implement?
options: Route logs to a Cloud Storage bucket using the Archive storage class.
Route logs to a Cloud SQL database.
Increase the retention of the _Default log bucket to 7 years.
correctAnswers: Route logs to a Cloud Storage bucket using the Archive storage class.

explanation.general explanation: Routing logs to a Cloud Storage bucket and applying the Archive storage class is the most cost-effective architectural pattern for long-term (multi-year) log retention for compliance data that is rarely accessed.

why other options are wrong.Route logs to BigQuery: While BigQuery is great for analytics, it is significantly more expensive for long-term cold storage compared to Cloud Storage Archive.
why other options are wrong.Route logs to a Cloud SQL database: Cloud SQL is an operational relational database. It is not designed or cost-effective for storing massive volumes of read-only log data.
why other options are wrong.Increase the retention of the _Default l: While you can increase log bucket retention, custom log buckets cost more per GB stored than the Cloud Storage Archive class.

questions.questionText: Your organization uses an external, third-party Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) tool like Splunk. You need to send all security-related Google Cloud logs to this external tool in real-time. Which routing destination should you configure in the Cloud Logging router?
options: Create a log sink to Cloud Pub/Sub
Create a log sink to BigQuery
Use Cloud Dataflow to pull logs
correctAnswers: Create a log sink to Cloud Pub/Sub

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Pub/Sub is a real-time messaging service. Creating a log sink to Pub/Sub is the standard architectural pattern for streaming Google Cloud logs to external third-party SIEM tools (like Splunk, Datadog, or Elastic) in real-time.

why other options are wrong.Create a log sink to BigQuery: BigQuery is used for internal historical analysis and SQL querying, not as a real-time streaming buffer for external SIEM tools.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud Dataflow to pull logs: Dataflow is for data processing. You can use Dataflow to read from Pub/Sub and push elsewhere, but the logging router destination itself must be Pub/Sub.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud Scheduler: Cloud Scheduler triggers jobs on a cron schedule. It does not route streaming log data.

questions.questionText: Your Node.js application running on Cloud Run frequently produces stack traces when it encounters unhandled exceptions. You want a service that automatically identifies these crashes, groups duplicate stack traces together, and alerts your development team. Which service provides this out-of-the-box?

explanation.general explanation: Error Reporting automatically aggregates and groups crashes and unhandled exceptions (stack traces) from your applications. It provides a centralized dashboard and can notify you when new errors occur.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace tracks request latency across microservices, not application crashes or stack traces.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler tracks CPU and memory allocation over time, not unhandled exceptions.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Audit Logs: Audit logs track 'who did what, where, and when' for Google Cloud resource configuration, not internal application stack traces.

questions.questionText: You need to ensure your external, customer-facing e-commerce website is available and responding with an HTTP 200 OK status from multiple geographic locations around the world. Which observability feature should you configure?

explanation.general explanation: Uptime Checks (in Cloud Monitoring) verify the availability of your web applications by making requests from multiple locations around the world and ensuring they return successful responses (like HTTP 200 OK).

why other options are wrong.VPC Flow Logs: VPC Flow Logs record network IP traffic going to and from VM instances. They do not actively probe a website for HTTP availability.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace tracks internal application latency, not external global availability probing.
why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy: IAP is a security tool for zero-trust application access, entirely unrelated to uptime monitoring.

questions.questionText: Your application writes simple text lines to stdout, which are ingested by Cloud Logging. You want to trigger an alert to your on-call team whenever the specific text string 'payment_failed' appears in the logs more than 5 times in a minute. How should you architect this?
options: Create a log-based metric in Cloud Logging and an alerting policy on it.
Use Error Reporting to catch the text string.
Use Cloud Trace to search for the string.
Create an Uptime Check configured to look for the string.
correctAnswers: Create a log-based metric in Cloud Logging and an alerting policy on it.

explanation.general explanation: Log-based metrics allow you to define a metric based on the occurrence of a specific filter or string pattern in Cloud Logging. Once the metric is created, you can use Cloud Monitoring to create an alerting policy when it crosses a threshold (e.g., > 5 times per minute).

why other options are wrong.Use Error Reporting to catch the text st: Error Reporting specifically parses recognized stack traces and unhandled exceptions, not arbitrary text strings like 'payment_failed'.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud Trace to search for the string: Cloud Trace is for distributed latency tracing, not for searching log text content.
why other options are wrong.Create an Uptime Check configured to loo: Uptime checks probe an application from the outside. While they can look for a string in an HTML response, they cannot search internal application logs.

questions.questionText: A critical Compute Engine VM was unexpectedly deleted in your production environment. You need to investigate and find out the exact IAM user identity that executed the deletion. Which specific Cloud Audit Log should you review?

explanation.general explanation: Admin Activity Audit Logs record administrative actions that modify the configuration or metadata of resources, such as deleting a VM instance. These logs are always enabled by default.

why other options are wrong.Data Access Audit Logs: Data Access logs record API calls that read the configuration or metadata of resources, or read/write user-provided data. Deleting a VM is a modification, not just a data read.
why other options are wrong.VPC Flow Logs: VPC Flow Logs record network traffic (IPs, ports, bytes), not the IAM identities executing administrative API calls.
why other options are wrong.System Event Audit Logs: System Event logs record actions initiated by Google systems (like a live migration), not actions initiated by user identities.

questions.questionText: Due to strict data privacy policies, your security team needs to track every time a user downloads or reads a sensitive customer file stored in a Cloud Storage bucket. Which type of log must you explicitly enable to satisfy this requirement?

explanation.general explanation: Data Access Audit Logs record API calls that read data or metadata. Because they can generate a massive volume of logs, they are disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled to track 'read' operations on objects like Cloud Storage files.

why other options are wrong.Admin Activity Audit Logs: These are enabled by default and track modifications (creations, deletions, updates), but they do not track 'reads' of user data.
why other options are wrong.System Event Audit Logs: These log events generated by Google's underlying infrastructure, not user-initiated data reads.
why other options are wrong.Policy Denied Audit Logs: These record when a user is denied access by VPC Service Controls, not successful reads of the data.

questions.questionText: You have deployed a fleet of Compute Engine virtual machines. While Google Cloud automatically monitors basic CPU and disk I/O, you also need to monitor the application logs and internal memory consumption of the VMs. What must you do to enable this observability?
options: Install the Ops Agent on the VM.
correctAnswers: Install the Ops Agent on the VM.

explanation.general explanation: The Google Cloud Ops Agent is required to collect telemetry from inside the operating system of a Compute Engine VM. It gathers application logs, system logs, and deep metrics like RAM utilization and sends them to Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring.

why other options are wrong.Enable VPC Flow Logs: VPC Flow Logs monitor network IP traffic at the VPC level. They do not collect application logs or memory metrics from inside the VM.
why other options are wrong.Install Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler analyzes code execution efficiency, not general OS-level syslog or generic RAM consumption.
why other options are wrong.Create an Uptime Check: An Uptime check hits the VM's external IP to see if it responds, but it cannot collect internal OS logs or memory metrics.

questions.questionText: Your network engineers suspect that there is a large volume of unauthorized network traffic occurring between two Compute Engine VMs located in the same VPC subnet. How can they verify the source IPs, destination IPs, and byte volumes of this traffic?

explanation.general explanation: VPC Flow Logs record a sample of network flows sent from and received by VM instances. They are used specifically to analyze network traffic volumes, troubleshoot connectivity, and identify source/destination IPs within a VPC.

why other options are wrong.Enable Firewall Rules Logging: Firewall Rules Logging only logs traffic that matches specific firewall rules. VPC Flow Logs are better for analyzing all general traffic volume between internal VMs.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace is for application-level latency tracing, not IP-level network packet analysis.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler looks at code execution (CPU/RAM), entirely unrelated to network traffic.

questions.questionText: Your application deployed on GKE writes a massive amount of low-value 'DEBUG' level logs, which is significantly increasing your Cloud Logging costs. You want to stop these specific debug logs from being stored in Google Cloud, while still retaining 'ERROR' and 'INFO' logs. What is the most efficient solution?
options: Configure an exclusion filter in the Cloud Logging router.
correctAnswers: Configure an exclusion filter in the Cloud Logging router.

explanation.general explanation: An exclusion filter configured in the Cloud Logging router allows you to discard logs that match a specific criteria (such as severity=DEBUG) before they are stored in log buckets, effectively reducing storage costs while keeping important logs.

Alerting notifies you of conditions; it does not stop logs from being ingested and billed.
Exporting routes a copy elsewhere. Without an exclusion filter, the logs will still be stored in the default bucket and incur costs.
why other options are wrong.Disable the _Default log bucket entirely: Disabling the default bucket would drop ALL logs (including ERROR and INFO), which violates the requirement to retain important logs.

questions.questionText: Your organization uses open-source Prometheus to monitor Kubernetes clusters. You want to migrate to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and continue using Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards, but you do not want the operational burden of managing the underlying Prometheus servers. Which observability service provides this?
options: Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus
correctAnswers: Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus is a fully managed, multi-cloud, cross-cluster observability solution for Prometheus. It allows you to use standard open-source Prometheus queries (PromQL) and Grafana without managing the infrastructure.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler is for continuous code execution profiling, not an open-source metric collection system like Prometheus.
why other options are wrong.Error Reporting: Error Reporting tracks unhandled exceptions, not general infrastructure and application metrics.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace tracks request latency, not Prometheus-compatible metric ingestion.

questions.questionText: You have created an alerting policy in Cloud Monitoring to trigger when CPU utilization exceeds 90%. You need the alert to automatically send a message to a specific Slack channel and trigger an incident in PagerDuty. How should you integrate this?
options: Configure Notification Channels in Cloud Monitoring.
Create a Log Sink to Cloud Storage.
Use Cloud Build to deploy a webhook.
correctAnswers: Configure Notification Channels in Cloud Monitoring.

explanation.general explanation: Notification Channels in Cloud Monitoring are explicitly used to define where alerts should be sent when an alerting policy triggers. Supported native integrations include Email, SMS, Slack, PagerDuty, Webhooks, and Pub/Sub.

A log sink simply stores raw text logs. It does not integrate with Slack or PagerDuty for real-time alerting.
Cloud Build is a CI/CD tool. While you could write a script, Cloud Monitoring natively supports Webhooks and Slack via Notification Channels without needing CI/CD pipelines.
Cloud Scheduler triggers time-based cron jobs, it does not respond to metric threshold alerts.

questions.questionText: Your site reliability engineering (SRE) team wants to formally measure and report on the reliability of your service, specifically targeting a 99.9% availability goal over a rolling 30-day window. Which feature in Cloud Monitoring allows you to formally define and track this metric?
options: Define Service Level Objectives (SLOs) in Cloud Monitoring
correctAnswers: Define Service Level Objectives (SLOs) in Cloud Monitoring

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Monitoring natively supports Service-Level Objectives (SLOs). You can define an SLI (Service Level Indicator, like availability) and set an SLO target (like 99.9%), allowing the system to automatically calculate error budgets and alert on burn rates.

why other options are wrong.Create custom dashboards: While dashboards can show metrics, the native SLO feature calculates error budgets and provides SRE-specific tracking automatically.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace measures latency across microservices, but it does not formally track SRE error budgets and SLOs.
why other options are wrong.Enable Data Access Logs: Audit logs track user reads; they are completely unrelated to measuring application availability goals.

questions.questionText: A developer cannot access a database VM in your VPC. You suspect that a specific internal 'deny' firewall rule is blocking the traffic. How can you verify exactly which firewall rule is dropping the packets?

explanation.general explanation: Firewall Rules Logging specifically allows you to log the network packets that are allowed or denied by individual VPC firewall rules. This is the exact tool needed to prove that a specific rule is blocking traffic.

why other options are wrong.Enable VPC Flow Logs: VPC Flow Logs sample traffic volume and IPs, but Firewall Rules logging explicitly provides the exact rule name that allowed or denied the connection.
why other options are wrong.Enable Data Access Audit Logs: These log API reads, not network traffic packets.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler tracks application code performance, not network traffic or firewalls.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud services form the foundational core of the operations suite, responsible for collecting metric data and text-based event records from Google Cloud resources? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Monitoring (for metrics, dashboards, and alerting) and Cloud Logging (for event logs, audit trails, and text records) are the two core foundational services of the Google Cloud operations observability suite.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Spanner: Cloud Spanner is a globally distributed relational database.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Data Fusion: Cloud Data Fusion is a data integration and ETL tool.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Armor: Cloud Armor is a web application firewall (WAF) and DDoS protection service.

questions.questionText: You are designing a centralized logging architecture. You want to route logs to specialized storage services using the Cloud Logging Router. Which two services are natively supported destinations for a Cloud Logging sink? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: The Cloud Logging Router natively supports routing logs to Cloud Storage buckets (for cheap, long-term retention), BigQuery datasets (for SQL analytics), Cloud Pub/Sub topics (for streaming), and other Log buckets.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is an operational relational database. Cloud Logging does not natively sink logs to it.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Spanner: Cloud Spanner is a distributed database, not a native log routing destination.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine provides VMs. You cannot route logs directly into a VM via the logging router; you would route them to Pub/Sub and have the VM consume them.

questions.questionText: If you do not configure any custom routing rules or exclusions, where are all standard application logs and non-audit logs stored by default in Google Cloud, and retained for 30 days?

explanation.general explanation: By default, Google Cloud automatically creates a `_Default` log bucket. All non-audit logs (like application logs, VPC flow logs, etc.) are routed here and retained for 30 days unless custom sinks or exclusions are applied.

why other options are wrong.The _Required log bucket: The `_Required` log bucket is automatically created to store Admin Activity and System Event audit logs. It retains them for 400 days and cannot be disabled.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage: Logs are not stored in a customer-visible Cloud Storage bucket by default; you must explicitly create a sink to send them there.
why other options are wrong.BigQuery: Logs are not stored in BigQuery by default; you must explicitly create a log sink to export them.

questions.questionText: Your team needs to understand the execution time of individual operations within an application. Specifically, they want to see how long a database query takes versus an external API call during a single HTTP request. Which observability tool tracks this latency breakdown?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Trace tracks the latency of incoming requests and allows you to instrument your code to create 'spans'. These spans show the exact execution time of distinct operations, like a database query or API call, within a single request.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler looks at CPU usage and memory allocation across the entire application process, not the step-by-step latency breakdown of a single HTTP request.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Monitoring: Cloud Monitoring shows aggregate metric data (e.g., average latency), not the specific internal breakdown of an individual request.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Logging: While you could write custom timestamps to logs, Cloud Trace is the purpose-built visual tool for distributed latency tracking.

questions.questionText: You are migrating a legacy application stack to Compute Engine. You need to collect deep performance metrics from third-party services running on the VMs, such as Apache web server and MySQL database metrics. What is the recommended approach to ingest these into Cloud Monitoring?
options: Install the Ops Agent and configure the third-party integration.
Write a custom Bash script to push metrics to Cloud Storage.
correctAnswers: Install the Ops Agent and configure the third-party integration.

explanation.general explanation: The Google Cloud Ops Agent includes built-in integrations for numerous third-party applications (like Apache, NGINX, MySQL, Redis). Installing the agent and configuring the specific integration is the standard way to send these specialized metrics to Cloud Monitoring.

why other options are wrong.Write a custom Bash script to push metri: Cloud Storage is for files, not time-series metric ingestion. The Ops Agent already handles this natively to Cloud Monitoring.
VPC flow logs only capture network IP packet data, not application-level metrics from Apache or MySQL.
Cloud Trace is for latency tracing, not for polling metrics from a MySQL database.

questions.questionText: Your business team wants a dashboard that displays the 'number of items currently in users shopping carts' across your e-commerce platform in real-time. Since this is a highly specific business metric, how should you get this data into Google Cloud?
options: Write custom metrics to the Cloud Monitoring API.
correctAnswers: Write custom metrics to the Cloud Monitoring API.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Monitoring supports custom metrics. If you have business-specific data (like 'shopping cart size') that isn't native to GCP infrastructure, your application code can use the Cloud Monitoring API to write these custom time-series metrics.

VPC Flow Logs only show network traffic, which cannot tell you business-level details like shopping cart items.
Audit logs track infrastructure modifications, entirely unrelated to application business logic.
Cloud Profiler tracks RAM and CPU usage of code execution, not business data like cart sizes.

questions.questionText: Your company has deployed a web application behind a global load balancer. To guarantee high availability, you need to be alerted immediately if the application stops serving traffic to users in Asia or Europe. Which monitoring pattern achieves this?
options: Create Uptime Checks configured for multiple geographic regions.
Use Cloud Trace to simulate traffic.
Check the Data Access Audit Logs.
correctAnswers: Create Uptime Checks configured for multiple geographic regions.

explanation.general explanation: Uptime Checks allow you to verify the availability of your URL or IP address. By selecting multiple geographic regions (e.g., Asia and Europe), Google's probing servers in those locations will continuously verify that your site is responding to users globally.

Cloud Trace records latency data generated by real requests; it does not actively simulate traffic or probe external endpoints.
Data Access logs track who read internal GCP resources, they do not verify external website availability.
While flow logs show traffic arriving, they do not proactively test application availability from a user's geographic perspective.

questions.questionText: Google Cloud infrastructure performs routine maintenance, which occasionally involves live-migrating your Compute Engine VMs. You want to see exactly when these live migrations occurred over the past month. Which Cloud Audit Log contains this information?

explanation.general explanation: System Event Audit Logs record actions that are generated by Google Cloud's automated systems, rather than by human user actions. A live migration is a system event executed by Google's infrastructure.

why other options are wrong.Admin Activity Audit Logs: These record administrative changes made by users (e.g., a developer deleting a VM), not automated infrastructure events by Google.
why other options are wrong.Data Access Audit Logs: These record users reading data, entirely unrelated to VM maintenance.
why other options are wrong.Policy Denied Audit Logs: These record security denials from VPC Service Controls.

questions.questionText: You want to receive an automated email notification if the CPU utilization of any virtual machine in your production project stays above 80% for more than 5 minutes. What is the correct observability workflow?
options: Create an alerting policy in Cloud Monitoring.
Create a Log Sink to Pub/Sub.
correctAnswers: Create an alerting policy in Cloud Monitoring.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Monitoring alerting policies allow you to define conditions based on metrics (like CPU > 80% for 5 minutes). When the condition is met, the policy triggers and sends notifications to configured channels (like email).

Log sinks route raw text logs, they do not calculate time-series metric thresholds.
Error reporting tracks unhandled code exceptions, not CPU utilization metrics.
Exclusion filters drop logs to save money; they have nothing to do with alerting on metrics.

questions.questionText: Your company is operating in Europe and must comply with strict data sovereignty laws. All application logs must be stored physically in the `europe-west1` region. How should you configure Cloud Logging to meet this requirement?
options: Create a custom Log Bucket in that specific region and route logs to it.
Default logs always stay in the region they are generated.
correctAnswers: Create a custom Log Bucket in that specific region and route logs to it.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Logging allows you to create custom Log Buckets in specific geographic regions (e.g., `europe-west1`). By creating a sink that routes your logs to this bucket, you ensure the log data physically resides in the required region.

VPC Flow Logs only capture network data; enabling them does not control the physical storage location of logs.
Cloud Trace is for distributed tracing, unrelated to the regional storage of log text.
why other options are wrong.Default logs always stay in the region t: This is false. The `_Default` bucket is often created in a global or pre-defined location depending on org settings, so relying on defaults without explicit regional bucket creation is risky for compliance.

questions.questionText: Security best practices dictate that fundamental audit trails must always be maintained. Which two types of Google Cloud Audit Logs are enabled by default and cannot be disabled? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud ensures a baseline of security auditing by having Admin Activity Audit Logs (which track administrative configurations) and System Event Audit Logs (which track Google infrastructure events) enabled by default. They cannot be turned off, and there is no charge for storing them in the _Required log bucket.

why other options are wrong.Data Access Audit Logs: These are disabled by default because they can generate massive volumes of logs and incur costs.
why other options are wrong.Policy Denied Audit Logs: These are enabled by default but are specific to VPC Service Controls, and the core un-disableable ones are Admin Activity and System Event.
why other options are wrong.VPC Flow Logs: These are strictly network logs and are disabled by default on subnets.

questions.questionText: Your networking team wants a highly visual map to see the architecture of your VPC networks and the actual traffic flow volumes between different Google Cloud regions and external internet locations. Which observability tool provides this visual mapping?
options: Network Topology in Network Intelligence Center
correctAnswers: Network Topology in Network Intelligence Center

explanation.general explanation: Network Topology is a feature of the Network Intelligence Center. It provides a visual, interactive graph showing your VPC architecture and actual traffic flows (throughput, packet loss) between regions, zones, and external networks.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace provides a waterfall chart of application latency across microservices, not a network infrastructure map.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler provides flame graphs of code execution inside an application, not network traffic visualizations.
why other options are wrong.Uptime Checks: Uptime checks monitor if a URL is responding. They do not map network architecture or visualize VPC traffic flows.
